transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’ve been having these late work nights where I order dinner, but then it turns into a whole entrée, sides, dessert, and then extra snacks from my kitchen. It’s way more than I’d normally eat if someone else were there with me.
During those eating episodes, do you feel unable to stop or control how much you’re eating?

Yes. Once I start, there’s a point where I’m still thinking I should stop, but I keep going anyway—opening another package or ordering more. It feels like the decision isn’t really in my hands anymore.
After these episodes, do you do anything to try to make up for the eating, like making yourself vomit?
I’m not sure what counts as making up for it. I don’t really know—I just feel bad afterward.
After you eat this way, do you ever make yourself vomit?
No, I don’t make myself vomit afterward.
After these eating episodes, do you ever use laxatives, diuretics, or other medicines to try to get rid of the calories?
I’m not really sure what you mean by other medicines. I don’t think I’ve noticed myself doing anything like that.
After these eating episodes, do you deliberately go without eating for a long time to make up for it?
I don’t think so. I might feel like I should skip something afterward, but I haven’t really noticed myself deliberately going without food for a long time.
After these eating episodes, do you ever exercise hard to try to burn off the calories?
No, I haven’t noticed myself doing that.
Do these eating episodes upset you a lot?
I’m not sure. I guess I feel bad afterward sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d say it upsets me a lot.
How often do these eating episodes happen?
When I look back at my delivery receipts and calendar, it seems like it happens at least one night a week, sometimes more. It’s been that way for several months.
When these episodes happen, do you eat what most people would consider an unusually large amount of food for the situation?

Yes. On late work nights, I’ll order dinner, but then it turns into the whole entrée, sides, dessert, and snacks from my kitchen too. It’s way more than I’d normally eat, especially if someone else were there.
Do these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress?
I’m not really sure how to judge “a lot.” I do feel bad afterward sometimes, but I haven’t thought of it as something that upsets me constantly.
When these episodes happen, do you usually eat alone because you feel embarrassed about how much you’re eating?

Yeah, usually. I’m careful to eat lightly around coworkers or friends, but when I’m alone in my condo after midnight, I’ll close the blinds. I get rid of the delivery containers quickly too—I’d be really embarrassed if anyone saw how much food there was.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit to try to get rid of the food?
No, I don’t make myself vomit afterward.
Do these eating episodes feel very upsetting to you?
I’m not sure I’d say very upsetting. I do feel ashamed afterward sometimes, but it’s not like I’m thinking about it all the time.
Do these eating episodes cause you marked distress?
I’m not really sure what counts as marked distress. I feel ashamed sometimes afterward, but I wouldn’t say it’s overwhelming or constant.
During these episodes, do you eat much more quickly than you normally do?

Yeah. When it happens, I eat really fast at my desk—barely taste anything, just go from one container to the next while I have Illustrator open. Then a few minutes later I realize I’ve eaten most of it.
During these eating episodes, do you keep eating until you feel uncomfortably full?
Yes. By the end I’m often so full my stomach feels tight against my waistband, and I have to sit really still on the couch before I can even clean up the takeout bags.
Would you say these eating episodes cause you significant distress?
I’m still not sure I’d call it significant. I do feel ashamed afterward sometimes, but it’s not like I’m distressed all the time.
Do these eating episodes feel deeply upsetting to you?
I don’t know if I’d say deeply upsetting. I feel bad about it afterward, embarrassed sometimes, but in the moment it’s more like I don’t really think about how I feel.
During these episodes, do you eat even when you’re not physically hungry?
Yes, a lot of the time. I’ll have had a normal dinner and not really feel hungry, but then I’m still going into the kitchen or ordering delivery while I’m trying to finish a project.
